prerequisites: Scientific-technical knowledge from basic subjects such as Chemical Fundamentals (1st year)
Scientific-technical knowledge from basic subjects such as Materials Science (2nd year)
Scientific-technical knowledge from basic subjects such as Thermal Engineering (2nd year)

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Capacity to manage mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards.
Capacity to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Capacity to apply quality principles and methods.
Knowledge, understanding, and capacity to apply necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Adopt a responsible, orderly work attitude and be willing to learn, considering the challenge posed by continuous training.
Apply the strategies of the scientific methodology: analyze the qualitative and quantitative situation and problems. Formulate hypotheses and solutions using industrial engineering models.
Work effectively in a group, integrating capacities and knowledge to make decisions in the field of industrial engineering.
Analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions to the challenges posed by technological development, applying sustainability criteria.

Know, understand, and apply the mandatory legislation, specifications, regulations, and standards in the exercise of the profession of industrial technical engineer, being consistent with professional ethics and applying quality, safety, and business economic framework principles and methods.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to environmental pollution. What is the environment? What is pollution? United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Environmental regulations and legislation. IPPC and application instruments.

Atmospheric pollution. The atmosphere. Types of pollutants: Primary and secondary pollutants. Effects of pollution. Macroecological aspects: Climate change, acid rain and ozone layer. Regulatory framework. Immission limit values and air quality. Atmospheric stability. Dispersion of pollutants through chimneys (Gaussian model). Technologies for controlling particle and gas emissions.
Noise pollution: Characterization: physical properties of sound. Measurement, propagation, and control of noise. Applicable legislation.

Water pollution. Physico-chemical properties of water. Origin, classification and characterization of pollutants. Pollution indicators. Effects produced by discharges. Treatment of natural waters: description of a Drinking Water Treatment Plant (ETAP) and water treatments for industry. Wastewater treatment: Wastewater Treatment Plant (EDAR). Industrial wastewater treatment (ARI). Reuse of treated wastewater. Water quality criteria. Regulatory Framework.

Waste and soil. Origin, classification and characterization of waste. Urban waste (RU) and its management. Valorization of RU. Hazardous waste (RP): origin and classification. RP identification system. RP treatment systems. Waste disposal: landfills. Regulatory framework. Soil contamination and remediation.
Environmental management. Environmental management systems: EMAS Regulation. Differences between ISO 14001 and EMAS.
teaching_methods: Individual tasks on scientific articles, institutional reports, regulations, specific information links
assessment_rules: Assessment can be continuous or final. Continuous assessment comprises a mid-semester partial exam (31%), a January final exam (49% or 80% depending on partial result), and individual/team tasks (20%). The January final exam must be passed for continuous assessment, otherwise the final grade is limited to its score. Students may opt for a 100% final written exam in January (ordinary call) or June (extraordinary call, where task grades may be optionally kept for an 80% exam).
